narrative.overview:
Chatmail is mail, so the site arrives as an airmail envelope. Every surface is a piece of postal paper: the envelope face framed by red-and-blue chevron bands, one perforated sheet of stamps (the four projects with a live site carry its screenshot, the rest carry an engraved two-colour vignette), an aerogramme edged with chevrons, CN 22 customs-declaration slips for the install commands, a route map with its key, a registered-mail slip for funders, and, to close the page, the back of the envelope with the return address on its flap. The postal vocabulary is the system, not ornament layered on a generic page; new surfaces should be another piece of mail (a slip, a label, a stamp, a form) before they are a card or a panel.

The material is flat paper and printed ink. Depth comes from paper tone steps (paper, paper-2, paper-3) and from things being stuck on slightly crooked (the hero stamp at 4deg, the PAR AVION label at -2deg, the registered slip at 1.5deg, the envelope back at -0.8deg), never from shadows at rest. Colour is postal: near-black ink on white or cool-grey paper, with airmail red as the brand voice and airmail blue as its second. Lettering borrows from stamps: heavy extra-condensed capitals for display, a warm humanist sans for reading.

Density is generous and editorial: a full-viewport envelope, wide section gaps, one reading column per section, each section composed on its own grid (see Layout). Every locale is first-class, including RTL Persian, and the whole site works offline as a WebXDC mini-app, so every font and image is self-hosted.
keyCharacteristics: Postal-object vocabulary: envelope, stamp sheet, postmark, aerogramme, customs slip, route map, registered slip, return address.
Flat paper tone steps for depth; one shadow in the whole system, on the floating language menu.
Square corners everywhere; perforations and postal circles are the only non-rectilinear edges.
Red and blue airmail chevrons as the signature pattern.
Extra-condensed uppercase display, humanist sans text, Vazirmatn for Persian.
Strong ease-out motion, short durations, press feedback, hover only for fine pointers.

rules.name: The Dark-Desk Rule
rules.body: Dark mode darkens the desk, not the mail. The page ground, nav, section text, route map and stamp-sheet heading follow the theme; every postal object carries the global `.sheet` class, which sets `color-scheme: light` so every `light-dark()` token inside resolves to its light value, and maps `paper`/`paper-2`/`paper-3` onto the per-theme `sheet` steps and `red` onto `sheet-red`. The carriers are the envelope frame, the stamp-sheet selvage and each stamp's paper, the aerogramme, both CN 22 slips, the registered slip, the route's flying letter glyph and the envelope back in the footer; the standalone 404 slip follows the same rule with its own inline tokens. FAQ cards do the same by hand (`color-scheme: light; background: var(--sheet-2)`). The footer inverts the rule on purpose: it sets `color-scheme: dark` on a fixed `#0c0e12` desk in both themes, with the `.sheet` envelope back lying on it. Paper stays paper; it only dims a little at night.

rules.name: The Scheme-Fixed Field Rule
rules.body: Red and blue fields (the action button, the funding section, stamp faces, PAR AVION, the selvage colour checks) and the registered-mail slip keep the same colours in light and dark. They are printed matter, not themed UI.

rules.name: The Postal Pair Rule
rules.body: Red and blue are the only chromatic colours. Red leads (actions, labels, emphasis); blue seconds it (the airmail label, stamp faces, status). Nothing else is introduced, and no gradient ever blends them; they meet only as hard-edged chevron bands.

rules.name: The Condensed-First Persian Rule
rules.body: Under `:lang(fa)` the display stack is `'Sofia Sans Extra Condensed Variable', 'Vazirmatn Variable', Tahoma`. Sofia carries no Arabic-script glyphs, so Persian falls through to Vazirmatn per glyph while Latin brand names (Madmail, Delta Chat, TheMadOrg) keep the condensed display cut and still fit their stamps. Persian headings take line-height 1.25 and zero tracking; Persian body takes line-height 1.8; the return-address motto drops its tracking.

rules.name: The Em-Not-Ch Rule
rules.body: `ch` is measured on the Latin display face, far narrower than Persian letters, so any heading width set in `ch` is re-set in `em` under `:lang(fa)` (the hero h1 goes from 12ch to 8em).

rules.name: The Literal-Only Mono Rule
rules.body: The monospace stack is used only for literal install commands in the customs slip's Contents field (`dir="ltr"`, `text-align: left`, one block per command line with a 2ch hanging indent so a soft-wrapped continuation never reads as a new command). It never sets labels, metadata, or UI.

rules.name: The Paper-Not-Light Rule
rules.body: No shadows at rest and no gradients anywhere. The one shadow belongs to a real floating overlay. If something needs to stand forward, step its paper tone or stick it on crooked.

rules.name: The Perforation Rule
rules.body: Perforation is a 10px dotted border in the colour of the ground beneath, carried as `--hole`, centred on the edge with a -5px inset. On the stamp sheet stamps butt together with no gap, so the perforation is the gutter: each stamp's `.paper::before` punches only its block-start row (`border-block-start`) and `.paper::after` only its inline-start column (`border-inline-start`), and the plate's own `::after` punches the outer block-end and inline-end edges. In a complete tiling every shared edge is the start edge of exactly one stamp, so each gutter carries exactly one row of holes. `--hole` is `paper-2`, the selvage's tone, so the holes read as punched through to the margin. The lone hero stamp on the envelope is perforated on all four sides by one `inset: -5px` dotted border in `paper`. Never draw perforation with images, masks, or radial gradients.

rules.name: The Chevron Rule
rules.body: The airmail band is the single `--airmail` SVG pattern, red `#d7262e` and blue `#1d3a8a` diagonals on paper, shown as a border by padding a paper object over the tile. It frames the envelope face, the envelope back and the 404 slip (40px tile), edges the aerogramme on all four sides (24px tile) and draws the route line (20px tile); the route key redraws it as polygons in its relay symbol. It is not used as a general divider.

dos: **Do** make every new surface a piece of mail: a slip, label, stamp, sheet or form, in paper and ink.
**Do** put the global `.sheet` class on every postal object so it stays light paper on a dark desk.
**Do** resolve themed colours through the `light-dark()` tokens and keep red and blue fields scheme-fixed.
**Do** set display type in Sofia Sans Extra Condensed, 800, uppercase, and keep Sofia first in the Persian display stack.
**Do** re-set any `ch` heading width in `em` under `:lang(fa)`.
**Do** perforate stamps on the sheet by their start edges only, in the `--hole` colour, and let the plate punch the outer end edges, so every gutter carries one row of holes.
**Do** let the return address and the postmark name what we make (Madmail, Bedrud, Madcore) and the org's motto.
**Do** use logical properties and flip directional glyphs under `:dir(rtl)`.
**Do** give every pressable element a press scale (0.94-0.985) and gate hover effects behind `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)`.
**Do** use `--ease-out` with `--dur-press` / `--dur-ui` / `--dur-enter`, and honour reduced motion.
**Do** self-host every font and image so the WebXDC build works offline.
donts: **Don't** cast shadows at rest or use gradients; the language menu is the only shadow.
**Don't** round corners; radius is 0 except circles that are postal (postmark, route nodes and cancellations, registration targets).
**Don't** use monospace for anything but literal install commands.
**Don't** localise the postmark or flip it with `scale: -1 1`; it is Latin and LTR everywhere, mirrored only by moving its ring.
**Don't** repeat a project's name on its stamp face; the stamp's h3 carries it.
**Don't** add colours beyond paper, ink, airmail red and airmail blue.
**Don't** add a generic scroll reveal; entrances belong to a postal object, and entrance states apply only under `html.js`.
**Don't** load fonts or images from the network.
